correctness.rationale: The full valuation/period/mean theorem survives. At 5 the nonsquare 2 gives the unramified quadratic ring. For γ=-α³, (γ-1)/5 ≡ √2, and the quartic Laurent functions restricted to the three n mod 3 classes have slopes 0,2,3 modulo 5 at first lift, respectively. A shift not divisible by 3 would equate distinct slopes on all t mod 5, even after accounting for a carry. In the middle class the derivative is a unit at every γ^t; Laurent Taylor terms of degree >=2 are divisible by (γ^q-1)^2. The identity v5(γ^q-1)=1+v5(q) follows by binomial lifting, proving the least periods for a>=2. For β=γ^j, j=±2,±4, the length 5^s geometric sum factors into s five-term sums with bases β^(5^i). Each factor is 5 mod 25, because the sum of the linear indices 0+1+2+3+4 is 10; the starting power is 1 mod 5. Thus block sums have the stated residue. The frozen final sliding difference only starts at index 1. The repaired proof uses the already established period P_a to translate the index-0 condition to P_a and closes the implication before using the period lemma. If k=3·5^(a-1)m, the mean residue is k modulo 5^a, hence the divisibility iff 3·5^a divides k for a>=2. An independent modular recurrence-state calculation (a,b)→(b,6b−a) found state cycles 6,30,150,750,3750,18750,93750 and least quartic periods 1,15,75,375,1875,9375,46875 at a=1,…,7. Over complete quartic cycles, prefix sums at every start checked k=1,…,100 and 3·5^a−1,3·5^a,3·5^a+1, as well as block means at s=0,…,6. This corroborates rather than proves the theorem.
